Title: Observer Pattern and B-Trees: A Detailed Examination

Introduction: Software design patterns and data structures are foundational. Observer pattern addresses change propagation; B-tree addresses efficient storage and retrieval. Both are ubiquitous.

Observer Pattern:
- Definition: one-to-many dependency, subject notifies observers.
- Components: Subject, Observer, ConcreteSubject, ConcreteObserver. Subject maintains list, attach/detach, notify. Observer has update method.
- Mechanics: When state changes, subject calls notify, iterates observers, calls update. Observers can pull or push data. Loose coupling.
- Complexity: attach/detach O(1) if using linked list or ArrayList? Actually ArrayList add O(1) amortized, remove O(n) if by index? But typical list. Notify O(n) where n observers. Space O(n). If observers do heavy work, total O(n * work). No inherent time complexity for state change except notification.
- When choose: Need multiple independent views of same data, event handling, UI, MVC, real-time updates. Avoid tight coupling. Alternatives: polling (wasteful, latency), callbacks (single, not scalable), event bus/pub-sub (more decoupled, asynchronous, but more complex). Observer is synchronous, direct, simple.
- Examples: Java Swing ActionListener, Android LiveData, DOM event listeners, Model-View-Controller, RxJS Observables (though more complex), .NET events.
